claims.text: The as-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles are homogeneous solid-solution alloys with a random distribution of all six elements.
Moderate thermal annealing in an inert or reducing atmosphere promotes selective surface segregation in PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles.
Annealing causes differential atomic mobility among Pt, Pd, Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os.
Differential atomic mobility during annealing enriches Pt, Pd, and Ir at the nanoparticle surface.
Noble-metal surface enrichment modifies the local electronic density of the catalyst surface.
Changes in surface composition and electronic structure alter the adsorption energies of catalytic intermediates.
Optimizing intermediate adsorption reduces activation barriers for ethanol oxidation.
Annealed PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts will have higher ethanol-oxidation current densities than the as-synthesized baseline.
Annealing will produce measurable shifts in the binding energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The binding-energy shifts caused by annealing will indicate more favorable adsorption and be associated with enhanced reaction rates.
The proposed effect should hold for electrochemical ethanol oxidation in either acidic or alkaline media from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
The proposed effect requires annealing conditions that avoid nanoparticle sintering.
The proposed effect may not persist under extreme thermal treatments or non-electrochemical reaction conditions.
The magnitude of activity enhancement and the degree of segregation depend on annealing parameters and electrolyte environment.
Failure of annealing to produce both statistically significant noble-metal surface enrichment and corresponding activity or binding changes would falsify the hypothesis.
